conventions.convention: QMD uses supplied finite-valued density representatives relative to one sigma-finite dominator, an open finite-dimensional parameter set, and an interior base point. It asserts neither pointwise differentiability nor local mutual absolute continuity.
QMD information is the score second-moment matrix; singular information is permitted in the definition, whereas both regular likelihood theorems require positive-definite information.

The likelihood-ratio statistic is twice the unrestricted-minus-null maximized log likelihood. Regular equality nulls have tested coordinates ψ=0 and codimension q; efficient information is the nuisance Schur complement.
When q=d, nuisance blocks are empty and their products are zero. A Wald or score statistic whose displayed estimated inverse does not exist is set to zero.
The pointwise log-density score at the base point must agree almost surely with the QMD score; this compatibility is an explicit assumption.

Regular calibration assumes compact-uniform local likelihood and normalized score expansions, consistent estimated covariance/projection/information, and consistent measurable exact full and constrained maximizers. QMD alone is not asserted to supply the score expansion.
AC is assumed for the probability suppliers used by the likelihood theorems and normal examples. The QMD definition itself uses a supplied density family without invoking choice.
The boundary counterexample tests μ≤0 in the full model Θ=R at μ=0; the boundary belongs to the null, not the full parameter space.

load_bearing.statement: QMD at θ₀ means a measurable square-integrable score s satisfies the square-root-density expansion with squared L² remainder o(‖h‖²). Its information is Eθ₀[ssᵀ].

Assume AC, iid sampling at an interior point of an open dominated finite-dimensional model, QMD with positive-definite information I, a common-full-set local log-density Lipschitz envelope L with Eθ₀L²<∞, and a consistent measurable exact MLE. Then √n(θ̂ₙ−θ₀)=I⁻¹n⁻¹/²Σᵢsθ₀(Xᵢ)+oP(1) ⇒ N_d(0,I⁻¹). Under the same local hypotheses, every consistent measurable exact likelihood maximizer over a possibly n-dependent subset containing θ₀ is root-n bounded in probability.
Defines Lₙ=2{ℓₙ(θ̂ₙ)−ℓₙ(θ̃ₙ)}, Wₙ=nψ̂ₙᵀV̂ψ,ₙ⁻¹ψ̂ₙ, and Sₙ=Ueff,ₙᵀÎeff,ₙ⁻¹Ueff,ₙ with Ueff,ₙ=Uψ,ₙ(θ̃ₙ)−ĈₙUη,ₙ(θ̃ₙ), using the specified regular-null coordinates and consistent estimators.

Let a dominated finite-dimensional parametric model be quadratic-mean differentiable, with the supplied density family of def-qmd-path, at an interior point θ₀, with square-integrable score sθ₀. Then Eθ₀sθ₀=0.

Under AC and the stated correctly specified iid, regular equality-null, positive-information, full-MLE, constrained-MLE, compact-uniform likelihood/score expansion, and estimator-consistency hypotheses, Wₙ=Tₙ+oP(1), Sₙ=Tₙ+oP(1), and Lₙ=Tₙ+oP(1), where Tₙ=rₙᵀIeff⁻¹rₙ and rₙ=Δψ,ₙ−IψηIηη⁻¹Δη,ₙ. Each statistic converges under the null to χ²_q.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 says, “the supremum of absolute values is convex in the ghost sample vector.” Convexity need not hold in the observations X′ᵢ for nonlinear log-density increments. The intended conditional Jensen argument applies to the vector of evaluated criterion functions: sup_t|a_t−b_t| is convex in b. That elementary formulation supplies the stated symmetrization inequality.

alerts.finding: F7 attributes “Integrating a continuous derivative along an interval recovers the endpoint difference” to thm-ftc-first-part, and Proof 1.1 uses it for (g_t−g_0)/t=∫₀¹∂θg_rt dr. The opened supplier instead states that the integral function of an integrable f has derivative f at continuity points. The endpoint-difference identity is the statement of thm-ftc-second-part. The calculation is sound, but this citation reverses the supplied FTC direction without stating the elementary additional argument.

seams_checked.note: The pointwise score convention is imported with explicit compatibility with the QMD score. The batch does not import common-support differentiation identities as consequences of QMD.
Opened stochastic-order and vector Slutsky suppliers retain fixed finite-dimensional norms, probability convergence, and the absence of an independence requirement.

This is a contextual prerequisite. The batch assumes consistency and proves its needed local empirical-process bounds directly; it does not claim consistency or a uniform law from pointwise convergence.

This is a contextual prerequisite rather than an invoked Z-estimator or delta-method theorem. The MLE representation is established directly, and the calibration theorem states its score expansion explicitly.

The opened chi-square definition is used for the squared norm of a q-dimensional standard normal. Positive q and the distinction between asymptotic calibration and exact normal-model identities are preserved.

Opened QMD consumers retain square-integrable scores and allow singular information. Their LAN route normalizes the absolutely continuous component and controls singular and zero-overlap masses rather than asserting local mutual absolute continuity. The external Gaussian example's FTC citation issue is separately alerted.

The opened cone theorem explicitly assumes uniform local likelihood expansion and tight maximizers, retaining an interior full-model QMD point. The uniform endpoint counterexample correctly disproves QMD through gained support mass. Neither invokes regular equality-null chi-square calibration at a boundary null.
